texts.preamble: Bhalchandra Sevantilal Bhavsar vs State Of Gujarat on 2 February, 2023
texts.facts: It is the case of the petitioners that petitioners were partners of a partnership -firm running in the name and style of M/s. Food Island (Partnership) Firm a restaurant and Dhaba on National Highway No.8, Roli-Dungri, Tal.& Dist.Valsad 2.2 That on 27.04.2007, Respondent No.2 i.e. Food Inspector raided the premises of the petitioners i.e. petitioner no.6 and seized the samples of Paneer Tikka Masala under the requisite provisions of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 ('the Act', for short) and the sent the same for examination before the Public Analyst. 2.3 The Public Analyst submitted its report on NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/5670/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 02/02/2023 undefined 02.06.2007 and opined that the samples of Paneer Tikka Masala were adulterated. 2.4 Thereafter on 16.07.2014 the aforesaid report was made available to the petitioner as the same was served upon the petitioner and at the same time simultaneously the prosecution was launched against the present petitioners under section 16(i) (a) and 16(i) (a) (ii) of the Act against the present petitioners on 09.07.2014. 2.5 Being aggrieved by the aforesaid launch of prosecution after delay of seven years, the petitioners have approached this Court by way of the present petition and have prayed for quashing and setting aside the order dated 09.07.2014 passed by the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Valsad whereby the summons was issued to the petitioners in respect of Criminal Case No.2671 of 2014 so also for quashing and setting aside the entire proceedings of Criminal Case No.2671 of 2014. He drew attention of this Court to Section 13 of the Act and submitted that Section 13 provides that once the samples are collected and sent for examination to laboratory, on receipt of the report the result of the analysis was required to be sent to the present petitioner and on receipt of the said report it was open for the Bhalchandra Sevantilal Bhavsar vs State Of Gujarat on 2 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183631046/ 2 petitioner to approach the Court by way of an application within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of copy of the report to get the samples of articles of food kept by the Local (Health) authority analyzed by Central Food Laboratory. 3.2
texts.arguments: Learned advocate Mr.Chhaya submitted that in the instant case, samples were taken in the month of April, 2007 to be precise on 27.04.2007 and the report came on 02.06.2007 and despite the availability of the report with the Respondent No.2 the same was sent to the petitioner only on 16.07.2014 after the Court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate issued summons to the petitioner on 09.07.2014 i.e. after delay of more than seven years. He submitted that considering the NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/5670/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 02/02/2023 undefined fact that samples were of Paneer Tikka Masala, the petitioner's valuable right to refer the sample and result to Central Laboratory is severely affected because of this inordinate delay and, therefore, as the delay has not been explained, entire proceedings would be vitiated and hence the same may be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Learned advocate Mr.Chhaya relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Municipal Corporation of Delhi vs. Ghisa Ram reported in AIR 1967 SC 970, the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in similar set of facts, [LEAKAGE_MASK] and [LEAKAGE_MASK] the proceedings under Food Adulteration Act and by relying upon the same learned advocate Mr.Chhaya prayed for quashing and setting aside the entire proceedings in respect of the present petitioners as well. 4.1 Learned Additional Public Prosecutor Ms.Mehta though vehemently opposed the issuance of summons by the court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate vide order dated 09.07.2014 on the ground of public health, she could not explain the delay of seven years in NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/5670/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 02/02/2023 undefined launching the prosecution against the present petitioners after the report was available from 02.06.2007. She also could not dispute the fact that report was available for the first time to the petitioners only on 16.07.2014 i.e. almost after seven years after the report of the Public Analyst was received by Respondent no.2 indicating that the food samples were adulterated. 4.2 , in similar set of facts, the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed as under: " In Municipal, Corporation, Gwalior, v. Kishan Swaroop, (2) it was held that, where there was delay in launching the prosecution, it deprived the accused of the valuable right to challenge the report of the Analyst in the manner prescribed by s.13(2) of the Act, and when this right was denied to the accused for no fault of NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/5670/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 02/02/2023 undefined Further, Section 13 of the Act provides as under: "13. Report of public analyst. - (1) The public analyst shall deliver, in such form as may be prescribed, a report to the Local (Health) Authority of the result of the analysis of any article of food submitted to him for analysis. (2) On receipt of the report of the result of the analysis under sub-section (1) to the effect that the article of food is adulterated, the Local (Health) Authority shall, after the institution of prosecution against the persons from whom the sample of the article of food was taken and the person, if any, whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed under section 14A, forward, in such manner as may be prescribed, a copy of the report of the result of the analysis to such person or persons, as the case may be,
